_what: Where every D4 fixture comes from, so a reader can tell recorded evidence from a written-by-hand payload shape.

anj_block_page.html.from: France (the machine this repository is built on)
anj_block_page.html.what: The block page of the Autorite Nationale des Jeux, served verbatim with status 200 and content-type text/html in place of the Gamma JSON. 14547 bytes, UTF-8, unmodified.
anj_block_page.html.why_it_matters: Nothing at the HTTP level says the request failed, so only the body identifies the block. This file is what the detector is tested against.

anj_block_response.json.how: The same curl for the status and the headers, httpx 0.28.1 on CPython 3.12.1 for the TLS failure and its cause chain, ssl.getpeercert(binary_form=True) plus socket.gethostbyname for the certificate names and the address
anj_block_response.json.what: The response envelope, the resolved address shared by the three Polymarket API hosts, the certificate's DNS names (*.anj.fr, anj.fr) and the exact exception chain httpx raises without -k.
anj_block_response.json.why_it_matters: The certificate path and the body path are two different signatures of one block, and CPython 3.12 does not name the certificate in its message: the test needs the real strings to pin the detector against.

written_by_hand.why: Gamma and the CLOB cannot be recorded from this machine at all: every request to gamma-api.polymarket.com, clob.polymarket.com and data-api.polymarket.com is answered by the ANJ block above, so there is no real payload to capture. Recording them would take a run from another jurisdiction or through PMX_HTTP_PROXY, which the live test behind PMX_LIVE=1 is there to do.
written_by_hand.shapes: Fields and spellings are the ones the provider documents and uses: Gamma sends outcomes, outcomePrices and clobTokenIds as JSON strings, spells its instants three ways in one payload (2026-03-31T12:00:00Z, 2026-03-31 18:05:00+00, 2026-02-25T09:14:02.517Z), nests events[] with its own slug, category and tags, and answers /markets with a bare array. The CLOB answers /prices-history with {"history": [{"t": <unix seconds>, "p": <decimal in [0, 1]>}]}.

written_by_hand.prices: Every price is a JSON number and is parsed with json.loads(..., parse_float=Decimal): the importer never lets a float reach a mapper, and one test asserts that a float that does is refused.
